evidenceHint.en: Policy walkthrough record: each handled report against the policy's steps, every departure found and whether the policy or the practice was changed

templates.title: Vulnerability response and patch SLA
templates.description: Assess and prioritize each vulnerability by risk and plan and implement remediations within defined SLAs. Implements SSDF RV.2.

title.en: Record the method used to assess a vulnerability's risk and the inputs it takes

description.en: Prioritisation only holds up if two people reach the same answer, so write down how a vulnerability is assessed: the scoring input taken from the advisory, and the local factors that modify it — whether the affected code is reachable in the product, whether the deployment exposes it, what data it touches, and whether a mitigation is already in place. State how the assessed result maps to a severity band. Attach the assessment method.

evidenceHint.en: Vulnerability assessment method: the inputs taken, the local factors that modify them and how the result maps to a severity band

title.en: Record the remediation deadline set for each severity band

description.en: The control commits to defined remediation timescales, so define them: for each severity band, the time allowed from confirmation to a fix or mitigation being available, and separately to it reaching deployed installations, which is usually the longer and more often missed of the two. Record what happens when a deadline cannot be met and how that is escalated. Attach the remediation timescales with a deadline stated against each band.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation timescales: the deadline for each severity band to fix and to reach deployed installations, and the escalation route when one cannot be met

title.en: Assess each open vulnerability and record its severity, affected versions and planned response

description.en: Apply the method to every confirmed vulnerability and record the result: the severity reached, the local factors that moved it, the affected versions and components, the deadline that follows from the band, and the planned response — fix, mitigate, or accept with the reasoning. A vulnerability with no planned response is not assessed, only logged. Attach the assessment record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment record per vulnerability: the severity reached, the factors applied, the affected versions, the deadline and the planned response

text.en: Apply the assessment method to each confirmed vulnerability.
Record the local factors that moved the score up or down.
Record the affected versions and components for each entry.
Record the planned response and the deadline it falls under.

title.en: Deploy the fix or mitigation and record the version that closed each vulnerability

description.en: Carry out the planned response and record what actually closed each vulnerability: the release version carrying the fix, or the mitigation applied and where. Link the entry back to the report and the assessment so the chain from receipt to closure is traceable in one place. Where a mitigation is standing in for a fix, record it as still open with the residual risk rather than closing the entry. Attach the remediation record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record: each vulnerability with the release version or mitigation that closed it, linked back to the report and assessment

text.en: Implement the planned fix or mitigation for each vulnerability.
Record the release version carrying the fix.
Link the entry back to the original report and its assessment.
Keep entries closed by mitigation open with the residual risk recorded.

title.en: Notify the parties affected by a remediation through the route the disclosure process names

description.en: When a remediation ships, tell the people who need to act on it: the acquirers and users running affected versions, and the reporter who raised it. Record who was notified, by what route, on what date, and what they were told — the affected versions, what to do, and any interim mitigation. Where notification was deliberately withheld or delayed, record that and the reasoning. Attach the notification record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Notification record: who was notified, the route and date, what they were told, and the reasoning behind any withheld or delayed notification

title.en: Measure the remediations completed against the deadline for their severity band

description.en: Set the closures in the period against the deadlines their bands carry, and report both the ones met and the ones missed with the age of each. Include the vulnerabilities still open past their deadline, which are the ones an aggregate of completed work hides entirely. Record the reason behind each miss, since repeated misses in one band usually mean the deadline or the capacity is wrong rather than the individual case. Attach the performance report for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation performance report: closures against the deadline for their band, every miss with its reason, and every vulnerability still open past its deadline

templates.title: Root-cause analysis and SDLC improvement
templates.description: Analyze vulnerability root causes, look for patterns and similar defects, and update the SDLC to prevent recurrence. Implements SSDF RV.3.

title.en: Record the criteria that decide which vulnerabilities receive a root-cause analysis

description.en: Analysing everything is unaffordable and analysing nothing is what happens instead, so write the criteria down: which vulnerabilities get a root-cause analysis, by severity, by whether they reached a release, or by whether the same shape has been seen before. Say what a completed analysis must record and where analyses are filed so they can be read together later. Attach the criteria with the analysis template.

evidenceHint.en: Root-cause analysis criteria naming which vulnerabilities are analysed, with the template stating what a completed analysis must record

title.en: Record the root cause of each vulnerability that met the analysis trigger

description.en: For each vulnerability in scope, go past the defect to the cause: what was introduced, at which point in the lifecycle it entered, what allowed it in, and why review, analysis and testing did not catch it — the last question being the one that yields the improvement. Name a cause the organisation can act on rather than closing at human error. Attach the analysis record for each vulnerability analysed.

evidenceHint.en: Root-cause analysis record per vulnerability: the defect, where in the lifecycle it entered, what allowed it and why it was not caught

text.en: Establish the defect behind the vulnerability, not just its symptom.
Identify the lifecycle stage at which it was introduced.
Record why review, analysis and testing did not catch it.
Name a cause the organisation can act on rather than closing at human error.

title.en: Search the codebase for other instances of the defect class and record what was fixed

description.en: A confirmed vulnerability is a sample of a class. Search the codebase and the other products for the same shape — the same unsafe call, the same missing check, the same pattern in a different service — using a query derived from the analysis rather than reading by hand. Record what the search covered, what it found, what was fixed proactively and what was left with the reason. Attach the sweep record naming the class searched for.

evidenceHint.en: Sweep record: the defect class searched for, the codebases covered, the instances found, and what was fixed or deliberately left with the reason

text.en: Derive a search query from the analysis of the confirmed defect.
Run it across every codebase and product in scope.
Record each instance found and where it sits.
Fix the instances found proactively and record what was left, with the reason.

title.en: Group the recorded root causes and name the patterns they show over time

description.en: One analysis explains one vulnerability; the set explains the development process. Group the analyses gathered so far by cause — a coding practice not applied consistently, a lifecycle stage where defects repeatedly enter, a component or team carrying more than its share — and name the patterns with the evidence behind each. Say plainly where the sample is too small to support a pattern, rather than promoting a coincidence. Attach the pattern analysis.

evidenceHint.en: Pattern analysis grouping the recorded root causes, naming each pattern with the analyses supporting it and stating where evidence is too thin

title.en: Update the development practice each pattern points at and record what changed

description.en: Turn each pattern into a change somewhere in the way software is developed here — a coding standard rule, a reviewer checklist item, an automated check, a training module, a design guardrail — and record which was changed, by whom, and when it took effect. A pattern with no change recorded against it is where this control stops being a feedback loop. Where a pattern is accepted without change, record the reasoning. Attach the change record linking each pattern to what moved.

evidenceHint.en: Change record linking each identified pattern to the practice, check or training that was changed, when it took effect, or the reasoning for accepting it

pack.name: NIST SSDF Core Pack
pack.description: NIST Secure Software Development Framework — practices for producing software with fewer vulnerabilities.
